title: Aurora - Escalation Postmortem & Next Steps
summary: Follow-up postmortem for the 2026-07-28 production incident: brief timeline review, root cause (autoscaler edge case + KV cache warmup), mitigations applied (hotfix to autoscaler, emergency cache seeding), short-term reliability improvements, and agreement on pilot for dedicated capacity. Action items and dates captured.
next_steps: Redwood to share the full postmortem doc and the hotfix diff
Redwood SE to run dedicated-pool benchmarks and share latency/throughput spreadsheet
Customer to provide cluster logs and exact request IDs for the 07-28 window
Schedule a 2-week follow-up to review pilot metrics
Share SOC2/ISO artifacts and network diagram with Aurora security team
action_items: Marcus Hale: provide cluster logs + request ids for 2026-07-28 incident (due: 2026-08-05)
Priya Shah (Redwood SE): run latency and p99/p95 benchmarks of dedicated pool + quantization profiles and share spreadsheet (due: 2026-08-09)
Jamie Nguyen: send pricing/billing impact and pilot contract outline (due: 2026-08-06)
Samir Patel (Redwood Infra): implement autoscaler guardrail hotfix and coordinate deploy (due: 2026-08-04)
Lena Ortiz: confirm internal approvers and compliance checklist for private deployment pilot (due: 2026-08-10)
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-08-02 08:00 PT | Duration: 61 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Infra), Omar (CSM); Lena (Aurora VP Eng), Marcus (SRE), Priya R (Security), Diego (Platform), Anjali (Product)

[00:00] Jamie: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is the follow-up for the July 28th escal- escalation uh incident. we wanted to run through timeline, root cause, what we patched, and next steps. i'll hand it to Priya to kick off with the timeline.
[00:22] Priya (SE): yeah thanks. so quick timeline, at ~10:41 UTC on 2026-07-28 we saw a spike in token latency and a cascade of queued requests. around 10:43 the autoscaler reacted but there was an edge case where min-replicas dropped below the safe threshold because of a concurrent scale down + churn with the dedicated pool. that left some requests routed to cold instances and the KV cache wasn't warmed - so you saw repeated kv cache misses.
[00:55] Marcus: yup totally, we saw the same on our side, lots of 504-ish timeouts and retries. there was a retry storm from app layer, which amplified the load.
[01:12] Priya R (Security): quick q — did any user data leave the VPC during the event? our compliance folks flagged egress concerns.
[01:25] Priya (SE): no evidence of egress; requests were staying inside the VPC and the control plane logs show no external data transfer. we did lose some request-level logs during the window because logging agent hit OOM, that's on our to-do.
[01:40] Jamie: i'll add that to action items, thanks.
[01:45] Lena: can you explain the autoscaler edge case in plain english? like why did it scale down below min?
[01:54] Samir (Infra): sure, long story short there's a race: the metrics collector reported lower CPU because many requests were queued before they hit the worker, then the decision path triggered a scale-down. concurrently, the health-check briefly flapped which made replicas appear unhealthy and the orchestration accepted the lower target. the scheduler then removed nodes before the KV cache and warmup finished. it's a known-ish scenario but our thresholds were tuned too aggressively for Aurora's bursty pattern.
[02:30] Diego: ah okay that explains the cold-starts, we saw a lot of sequential cold-start multipliers.
[02:40] Priya (SE): yes and another nuance — model KV cache warmup is sequence-length dependent; we saw long sequences, so cache population took longer, which made the cold penalty worse. plus our prefetch wasn't configured for this workload.
[03:05] Anjali: sorry to interrupt, you said prefetch? is that something we can tune without infra changes?
[03:12] Priya (SE): some of it yes — you can adjust prefix caching TTL and prefetch heuristics at the request router level, that's a config change. autoscaler fixes need infra deploy.
[03:28] Lena: what immediate mitigations did you push?
[03:33] Jamie: Samir, do you want to cover the hotfix?
[03:36] Samir (Infra): yeah. so immediate actions we took: 1) temporary lock to prevent scale-down below min-replicas for 30 minutes post-deploy; 2) emergency seed of KV cache on the effected nodes using a prioritised prewarm job; 3) raised logging agent memory to avoid OOMs and preserved logs for next run. we also pushed a small change to make the autoscaler consider queue-length as a hard signal so it won't scale in during high-queue windows.
[04:05] Marcus: the hotfix helped, latencies dropped after the seed finished, but we did see a second smaller blip during retry storms.
[04:18] Priya R (Security): can you share the hotfix diff and the audit log entries? security needs the exact diffs for the vulnerability review.
[04:28] Omar (CSM): we'll attach the diff and the control plane audit logs to the postmortem doc in the next 24 hours.
[04:36] Jamie: yeah i'll send the postmortem doc and the hotfix diff, and Samir will add the deploy timeline.
[04:44] [05:00] Priya (SE): next, root cause summary: primary cause was autoscaler race + aggressive downscale thresholds for Aurora's bursty workload. secondary contributor was KV cache cold starts amplified by long sequence lengths and lack of prefetch. tertiary was logging agent OOM which reduced observability during the window.
[05:18] Lena: does Redwood have an option for dedicated capacity? that would give us predictable throughput and avoid multi-tenant scale churn.
[05:26] Jamie: yes, we do Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools. for many customers the dedicated pool removes the autoscaler shock, especially if you pin min-replicas to a committed baseline. Priya, can you speak to performance differences?
[05:38] Priya (SE): sure; dedicated generally gives steadier p95/p99, lower variability. you pay for reserved capacity but you get predictable latency. our recommendation for Aurora's workload (bursty, long sequences) is a small dedicated pool sized for baseline traffic + a separate burst policy. we can run a benchmark with your representative traffic to size it.
[06:00] Diego: how long to get a pilot up? we need to check procurement too.
[06:06] Jamie: pilot can be as quick as 2 weeks if procurement approves. we'll need a purchase order for the reserved pool; I can send an outline.
[06:14] Marcus: on the technical side, we'd like to reproduce the incident with a controlled replay before we commit — we can provide traces and request logs.
[06:23] Priya (SE): that's perfect. if you share request ids and a small sample traces we can replay and run the same load against a dedicated pool and hosted pool to show diffs.
[06:33] Anjali: what about security: SSO, SAML, KMS for keys, everything we need for private deployment?
[06:41] Jamie: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, SAML SSO, and VPN/VPC peering options. Priya R: any blockers from security perspective?
[06:50] Priya R (Security): we need SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest details, and an architecture/network diagram. also confirm audit log retention and that the control plane has RBAC logs.
[07:03] Omar (CSM): we'll attach SOC2 excerpts and retention metadata to the postmortem.
[07:08] [07:30] — small cross talk — someone joining late: sorry im on;
[07:35] Jamie: ok moving on to longer-term mitigations...
[07:40] Priya (SE): longer-term, we recommend three things: 1) autoscaler behavior change - add queue-length as hard signal and raise min-replica floor for Aurora; 2) improve cache prefetching + heuristics (config change); 3) improve observability — move logging agent to a sidecar with memory limits and continuous log shipping to S3 for retention. additionally, we suggest a canary rollout strategy for autoscaler changes with traffic shadowing.
[08:12] Marcus: can you keep autoscaler changes behind a feature flag so we can test?
[08:18] Samir: yes, we'll gate the change and run it in canary for 48 hours then ramp.
[08:23] Priya (SE): also, small operational tweak — increase warmup priority for models that see long sequences; that'll reduce cold penalty. it's a config we can toggle without infra deploy.
[08:35] Lena: what's the cost impact of keeping higher min-replicas? we need to balance budget and reliability.
[08:42] Jamie: there's a tradeoff; we'll model a few scenarios and show projected monthly cost vs. estimated reduction in incidents. I'll include a simple model in the follow-up.
[08:53] Diego: also worth considering quantization to reduce per-token latency, but that's more of an engineering effort and could affect quality.
[09:02] Priya (SE): correct, quan-tization is a path but we should run evals for output fidelity. for this call I wouldn't recommend it as the primary mitigation.
[09:14] [09:30] Lena: ok, recapping what we need from Redwood: postmortem doc, hotfix diff, audit logs, benchmark plan, pricing/pilot outline. from us: logs, sample traces, procurement sign-off.
[09:44] Jamie: yep. quick note on retries — app layer retrier should use exponential backoff and jitter; we can share a best-practice guide.
[09:56] Marcus: we already use backoff but jitter may be missing in a few services, we'll audit.
[10:05] Omar (CSM): action owners and dates will be in the doc. we'll also set a follow-up in two weeks.
[10:12] [10:30] Priya R (Security): one more ask — if we do a private deployment, we need a network diagram showing egress paths, and confirmation that audit logs are tamper-evident.
[10:45] Jamie: noted, we'll include network diagram and retention + tamper evidence notes.
[10:52] [11:00] — small pause —
[11:10] Priya (SE): i'll talk through the benchmark plan briefly: we want Aurora to send a 5-minute representative trace with distribution of sequence lengths, concurrency, and any special request patterns. we'll run three experiments: hosted baseline, hosted w/ autoscaler hotfix, and dedicated pool. metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec throughput, tail spike frequency, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll share spreadsheet and raw logs.
[11:45] Marcus: timeline sounds good. if you can provide the test harness we'll run it in our staging network.
[11:53] Priya (SE): yes we'll provide a JMeter-style harness and a small script to replay traces.
[12:00] Jamie: ok last thing — can we agree on next steps and dates? i recapped earlier but let's confirm.
[12:08] Lena: yes please.
[12:12] Jamie: 1) Redwood sends postmortem + hotfix diff + audit logs by 2026-08-03. 2) Marcus to provide logs and request ids by 2026-08-05. 3) Redwood SE to run benchmark and share results by 2026-08-09. 4) Samir to deploy autoscaler guardrail hotfix by 2026-08-04. 5) follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-08-16 to review pilot metrics. everyone ok?
[12:40] Lena: yes that's fine.
[12:45] Marcus: ok thanks.
[12:48] Jamie: thanks all, we'll send notes and the doc shortly.
[12:52] [13:00] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription quality: some product names were transcribed poorly (KV cache -> K V cash), and acronyms were sometimes hyphenated (S-O-C 2), typical of automated speech-to-text. The transcript retains filler words and a few overlaps.
